France takes in more foreign visitors each year than it has citizens: 102 million in 2024. It has led this map for decades. It has never been the country that earns the most from them.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The 2024 order: France 102m, Spain 93.7m, the United States 72.3m, China 64.9m, Turkey 60.5m, Italy 57.7m. Four of the six sit on the Mediterranean.

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)
2/ Now the money map, which looks different. Inbound tourism earned the US about $215bn in 2024, Spain $106bn, the UK $84bn - and France, the most visited country on Earth, about $77bn. Fourth.

3/ The usual explanation is geography. France is ringed by Britain, Germany, Spain, Italy and the Benelux, so a large share of its arrivals are short hops from next door. A visitor who flies to Australia does not come for two nights.
4/ Hong Kong is the figure that breaks intuition: about 45 million arrivals against 7.5 million residents. Six visitors per resident, most of them crossing from the mainland a few kilometres away.

5/ Saudi Arabia is dark for a reason that isn't holidays. Nearly 30 million arrivals in 2024, driven heavily by Hajj and Umrah pilgrims. This map paints religious obligation and a beach fortnight the same colour.
6/ China posted the biggest single jump on the list: 35.5m arrivals in 2023 to 64.9m in 2024, up about 83% in one year. Almost all of it is the long tail of reopening rather than new demand.

7/ The hatching is the part worth reading. Russia and Australia show no figure here at all - yet Australia earned roughly $52bn from inbound tourism in 2024. On this map, blank means unreported, not empty.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
